name: Knife
desc: From simple pocket knifes and switchblades to tempered KA-BAR-style fighting knifes, these practical little blades are as much street-weapons as they are weapons for close-quarters-combat in real warzones. They are often highly concealable, extremely lightweight, practical and come in an unfathomable amount of different styles. In a pinch - or for some even as a primary style - they can even be thrown, making them extremely versatile tool in combat.

name: Baton
desc: Batons are clubs, made out of rubber, wood or flexible metals that are usually used by corporate security and police forces to brutalize anyone unfortunate enough to stand between them and the point they want to go. Even though the baton has a price tag attached to it, it is not overly difficult to find a wrench, a lead pipe or a pipe with a nail in it that does the job just as well. Some of them are even collapsible.

name: Stun Baton
desc: Stun Batons are standard riot-control weapons, often viewed as a symbol of corporate-government controlled police oppression, but still pragmatically useful to Shadowrunners. Stun Batons consist of a battery in the head of the weapon that discharges heavy electric shocks to anyone unfortunate enough to be hit with it. Usually, Stun Batons charge through induction and inform their users about their charge level.

name: Sword
desc: This is a sharp, heavy piece of metal designed to cut their targets wide open. Available in a wide variety of styles (wakizashi, seax, scimitar, jian, machete, and so on and so forth), these one-handed blades are not as formidable as a katana in the hands of trained street samurais, but substantially easier to hide.

name: Tomahawk
desc: These modern takes on classic Native American weapons give as much respect to their predecessors as they can while moving into the 21st century. Made from modern composites, balanced for throwing and optimized for maiming, these handy little things are popular among the urban tribal street gangs; especially the First Nations in Seattle, the Salish Rangers and the Sioux Wildcats are often very fond of these finely crafted killing tools.

name: Staff
desc: These large, heavy sticks are popular with magicians and monk-styled adepts going for the traditional look. Available in composite, hardwood, high-carbon steel and other materials.

name: Katana
desc: This isn’t your great-grandfathers traditionally made sword, chummer, but this doesn’t stop this weapon from being an extremely deadly tool in the right hands. Mostly popularized by trideos, the katana have become a cliched staple for the street samurai and shadowrunners in general. Everyone – including deckers and mages – carries one of these, which is why there are probably more katanas on the market than of any other weapon.
Katanas are rather heavy, and therefore wielded with both hands.

name: Polearm
desc: Polearms include all weapons that are, at their very essence, blades at the end of a very long stick. A polearm usually features an axe-head, a glaive, a spear point or a similar maiming implement. Due to their length, polearms are almost impossible to conceal, but usually provide an edge against other melee weapons, making them a popular choice against trolls or other large critters if firearms aren't an option.

name: Combat Axe
desc: This barbaric, two-handed tungsten-alloy monster may appear primitive, but can be even deadlier than a firearm in the hands of the heavily augmented cyber-monsters of the late 21st century. Available in single- or double-bladed styles. Go ahead, go medieval.

name: Monofilament Whip
special: Breach 1, Sunder, Unwieldy 4, Vicious 2, Special (see description)

name: Light Pistol
desc: Commonly seen in the pockets of city-dwellers, light pistols cover about any civilian-issued handgun.

name: Heavy Pistol
desc: The bigger, meaner brother of the pistol family. The heavy pistol utilizes bigger cartridges than its’ civilian counterparts (or even most SMGs, for that matter) and therefore pack a bigger punch than most other handguns. Shadowrunners, Corporate Agents and Drugged-Up Gang-Bangers alike favor these weapons as their main weapons in close quarters. Unlike their lighter counterparts, heavy pistols often require licenses and are not always completely legal to buy and carry.

name: Holdout Pistol
desc: Hold-out pistols are very cheap and concealable, making them perfect for sneaking into a meet or wearing as a back-up piece. Street-scum often carry these as a self-defense weapon. They don’t have much else going for them.

name: Taser
desc: This pacifists' weapon of choice fires small needles, that deliver a large electric shock through the attached wires into the unfortunate victim. Security forces, civilians and runners alike tend to carry these in order to non-lethally incapacitate their targets. Generally speaking, tasers are completely legal in almost all jurisdictions and surprisingly effective against armored targets, but require the re-cocking of the weapon after every shot. Some versions even come with inbuilt monitoring software to ensure that you do not accidentally kill your target, and get sued by their loved ones in the process. Just don’t expect gangers to carry these.

name: Mini-Crossbow
desc: Originally developed as a weapon for silent assassinations, various models of dart-shooters and pistol crossbows have hit the market after the widespread success of the Ranger Sliver. Surprisingly, due to the simple construction of a crossbow, the mini-crossbow sees widespread use as a lightweight sidearm among scuba divers and subnautical combat divers.

Mini-Crossbows are silent, adding [[sss]] to all Perception and Vigilance checks made to locate a concealed shooter. Mini-Crossbows also do not suffer penalties from being fired underwater, in zero-air- or zero-gravity environments. Mini-Crossbows must be reloaded after every shot, and can load a wide variety of arrowheads.

name: Dart Pistol
desc: Parashield and Narcoject have released a series of weapons that defined the industry standard for non-lethal dart pistols. Usually carried as a specialized sidearm of special forces teams in hostage situations, dart pistols shoot injection darts that deliver their payload on successful impact. Usually, that payload consists of a strong narcotic agent, but these darts can be filled with all kinds of toxins and drugs, if one so desires.

Dart pistols can never deal more than one wound, and do never case any Critical Injuries by themselves; instead, when a successful ranged combat check with the dart pistol delivers a wound to the target, the dart administers its’ payload. The target then makes a Resilience check with a difficulty equal to the severity of the administered narcotic. By default, the darts inject narcoject or a similar nerve agent, but when a character is using a custom payload, use the table “Effects, Severity & Scarcity” to determine the relevant statistics for the specific narcotic.

name: Assault Cannon
desc: These babies are the very definition of the word "overkill". Simply put, Assault Cannons are miniaturized versions of tank cannons, and provide enough firepower to plow through entire blocks of houses. While some of the cheaper models use an ungodly amount of propellant, higher-end models tend to be designed as railguns; they accelerate tungsten metal rods through the use of magnetic rails.

name: Shock Grenade
desc: These grenades, often nicknamed "stun grenades" or "flash-bangs" explode to create a bright, loud, shocking blast that is distributed equally over a large area.

name: Fragmentation Grenade
desc: These classic killing devices distribute shrapnel in a large area after the initial blast, seriously injuring soft targets.

name: High-Explosive Grenade
desc: HE-grenades are designed to deliver a rather small, concentrated explosion intended to blast through armor.

name: Molotov Cocktail
special: Blast 2, Burn 2, Limited Ammo 1, cannot be launched

name: EMP Grenade
desc: Electromagnetic pulse grenades are designed to be used against electronic equipment, specifically against communication devices, drones and vehicles, causing them to short-circuit and fail. Against metahumans EMP grenades are only really useful against targets possessing cybernetic augmentations, but they can really frag their lives up.

name: Smoke Grenade
desc: These little tubes release a heavy cloud of smoke through vents in their hull that prevent anyone to see through them by visual means. Smoke Grenades are usually hot, preventing people with Therm-Optic vision to see through the thick smoke. The smoke generated by these grenades does not disperse easily, even outside, unless exposed to rather strong winds or heavy rainfalls.

After a Smoke grenade detonates, everything within Short range of the grenade becomes obscured by fog (meaning that a single Smoke grenade is enough to fill about entire room with smoke). The thrower of the grenade can choose to get inside of the smoke at the time of detonation. People from outside of the smoke suffer [[ssss]] to all checks in order to perceive or target anything within or on the other side of the smoke. People caught within the smoke suffer the same penalty towards all people within and outside of the smoke, and must make an additional Average([[dd]]) Resilience check at the beginning of each of their turns that they start in the smoke, or suffer two strain. This counts as poison.

name: Gas Grenade
desc: Similar to smoke grenades, gas grenades do not disperse mostly harmless smoke, but instead disperse irritating or even harmful tear gasses and nerve agents. Gas grenades follow the same general rules as smoke grenades, but are generally see-through, and their effects are up to the toxin used in the grenade.
Smoke and Gas Grenades usually last for ten minutes, or an encounter. At the Gamemasters discretion, this time can be shortened in heavy winds or rains, or lengthened in especially stale conditions.

name: Fragmentation Missile
special: Blast 12, Limited Ammo 1, Blast applies to Short range
